details: The US Producer Price Index (PPI) data for October is expected to be released today, Friday, November 13, 2026, at 8:30 AM ET (13:30 UTC). Markets anticipate a 6.6% annual rise in headline producer prices, up from 6.3% in September. This report is crucial as it often signals future consumer price trends and will significantly influence the Federal Reserve's interest rate decisions. A hotter-than-expected reading could intensify inflation fears and put downward pressure on Bitcoin and other risk assets, while a softer print might ease worries and allow for a recovery in risk assets.
title: US PPI Data Expected Today, Influencing Fed Rate Plans

details: Bitcoin broke below the $73,000 support level on November 10, 2026, following hotter-than-expected US inflation data for October. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) increased 0.4% month-over-month, surpassing the 0.3% forecast, reinforcing concerns about persistent inflation and strengthening expectations of a potential Federal Reserve interest rate increase in December. Higher interest rates typically create less favorable conditions for speculative investments like cryptocurrencies.
title: US Inflation Data Exceeds Forecasts, Bitcoin Falls Below Key Support

details: Despite macroeconomic challenges, including recent US inflation data, institutional investors continue to expand their exposure to cryptocurrencies. Regulatory filings reveal that major financial institutions, such as Barclays and Citigroup, significantly increased their stakes in spot Bitcoin ETFs during the third quarter of 2026. This institutional accumulation is helping to offset selling pressure and supports Bitcoin's price above critical technical levels.
title: Institutional Bitcoin ETF Inflows Counter Macroeconomic Pressures

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has indicated that delays in approving necessary European Union legislation could postpone the potential launch of a digital euro beyond its targeted date of 2029. While preparations for a 12-month pilot program are still on track to begin in 2027, the ECB official Piero Cipollone urged lawmakers to finalize negotiations on the Single Currency Package by the end of 2026 to avoid further delays.
title: Digital Euro Launch Faces Delays Due to EU Legislative Hurdles
